name: Create and publish course
description: Happy-path: Instructor creates a new course from the Courses list, steps through a 5-step guided wizard (title/description, thumbnail, pricing, pricing details, outline method), then builds content (adds resources, video embed, quiz generated by AI), reviews the curriculum in the Setup guide, publishes the course and receives a launch confirmation with the sales link. Entry point: Courses list (logged-in instructor). Exit point: Courses list with the new course marked Published and a visible sales link. Assumes user is logged in with permission to create and publish courses and has files (image, resources) available for upload.
problem: User task: Create and publish a new online course so students can purchase and access it. From the user's perspective they expect a guided, linear setup that captures course metadata (title, description, thumbnail), pricing (one-time/payment options), curriculum (outline, lessons, embedded media), and optional AI assistance for outline and quizzes — then publish and get a shareable sales link. From the system perspective the UI enforces a step sequence in a modal wizard for initial metadata, provides upload and preview affordances for images, exposes pricing options and a pricing detail form, offers AI options to generate outlines and quiz questions, surfaces curriculum editing (lesson-level content, resources, quiz blocks), and requires a final publish confirmation. Final result: User-perceived outcome is a published course with curriculum and pricing visible; system-level outcome is a new product record created, curriculum items saved, pricing plan attached, course state changed to Published, and a public sales link generated.

Users can view and manage their school courses on this interface. They can use the 'Filter' button to narrow down the displayed course list based on chosen criteria. The search field enables users to quickly locate a specific course by typing its name or related keywords. 'Catalog Order' and the ascending order button allow users to sort the course list by different sorting rules. The 'Reorder' button likely enables drag-and-drop or manual reordering of courses.

Users can browse course details displayed in a tabular format, including the thumbnail, course name (clickable for more details or editing), author, creation date, sales figures, enrollment numbers, status, and access action menus through the three-dot icon. The status label visually indicates if the course is published or not.

The 'New course' button enables users to add a new course, opening a form or wizard to input course info. Pagination controls allow users to manage how many courses to view per page and navigate between pages.

Overall, the interface supports the workflow of creating, organizing, editing, and monitoring courses offered by the school. It provides clear access to important metrics (sales, enrollments), status management, and sorting/filtering to efficiently handle course listings.
